page: Vultr vx1-m-16c-128g-960s is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 16 shared vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 128.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 960 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core CPU performance, including stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, falls within the average range (middle 50%). Memory performance is strong, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25%, while raw memory bandwidth tests remain in the average tier. For specialized workloads, static web serving throughput and small-model LLM inference generation show strong to top-tier capabilities, whereas medium-model LLM inference and Redis SET operations perform at average levels.

Given its shared CPU allocation, this server offers a cost-effective profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. The high RAM-to-vCPU ratio combined with fast local NVMe storage makes it highly suitable for database hosting, caching layers, memory-bound data processing, and static web serving. However, the shared CPU model presents a tradeoff for sustained, high-utilization multi-threaded compute tasks, which may experience performance variability compared to dedicated instances.
